solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pressed your butterfly

parts.note: to sit on something is to press it down, so pressed gives sat
YR is the standard written abbreviation of your

explanation.surface: A collector pins down and presses your butterfly specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: The satyr is a brown butterfly of the family Satyrinae, named for the woodland creature of myth.

clue.text: Here I have ox in silicon dish

indicators.note: the pieces before this word are placed inside the chemical symbol that follows

parts.note: SI is the chemical symbol for silicon
for a British newspaper, here is the UK
taken as written
a yak is a long-haired Himalayan ox

explanation.surface: A diner boasts of having beef in a dish made with silicon, an unappetising picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here' as UK is the setter speaking from Britain, where the Telegraph is printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Sukiyaki is a Japanese dish of thinly sliced beef simmered with vegetables at the table.

clue.text: Film someone needing an ASBO?

definitions.meaning: Hitchcock's 1960 thriller of this title, set at the Bates Motel
an ASBO is a British Anti-Social Behaviour Order, imposed on someone behaving dangerously, such as a deranged person

explanation.surface: A film about a tearaway who ought to be served with an antisocial behaviour order.
explanation.walkthrough: An ASBO was a British court order restraining antisocial behaviour; the question mark admits the second definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Hitchcock's famous thriller has this title, and slang uses the word for a dangerously unstable person who might need restraining.

clue.text: Attempt softly to find cause of sleeping-sickness

parts.note: an attempt is a try
P, piano, is the musical direction for playing softly

explanation.surface: A researcher quietly tries to track down what causes sleeping sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tryp is short for trypanosome, the parasite spread by tsetse flies that brings on sleeping sickness.

clue.text: Wife to watch steak

parts.note: a wife is jocularly a rib, from Eve being made from Adam's rib
to eye something is to watch it

explanation.surface: A wife is asked to keep an eye on the steak cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: Rib for wife is an old joke from Genesis, where Eve is made from Adam's rib.
explanation.definitionFit: A rib-eye is a cut of beef from the rib section, prized for its marbling.

clue.text: He's left one putting things together and introduced work for Mark, for example

indicators.note: work is brought into the shortened word, so it goes inside
the letters of He's have left, so they are taken out of the longer word

parts.note: a person who combines parts into a whole is a synthesist
the letters of he's, ignoring the apostrophe
OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Someone who combines things has departed, and a work is introduced for Mark, perhaps a gospel commentary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's left' looks like a person leaving, but it says the three letters of he's are removed; 'introduced' then puts the work inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew, Mark and Luke are the synoptic gospels, so Mark is an example of a synoptist, a writer of one.

clue.text: Flawed reasoning to weep about when you heard it about saint

indicators.note: the weeping word goes around everything that follows

parts.note: to weep is to cry
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: you said aloud is just like the letter U

parts.note: the word whose sound gives a single letter

indicators.note: the pronoun it is placed around the abbreviation for saint

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone weeps on hearing sophistry about a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: There are two 'about's: the first wraps the weeping word round everything else; the second wraps 'it' round the saint's letter. 'heard' turns 'you' into a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Casuistry is clever but unsound argument, especially about moral questions, so it is a kind of flawed reasoning.

clue.text: Fortune-teller is coming back via Luxembourg

indicators.note: the word is returns, reading the other way

parts.note: via means by way of, so by
L is the international vehicle code for Luxembourg

explanation.surface: A fortune-teller is returning home by way of Luxembourg.
explanation.definitionFit: In antiquity a sibyl was a woman who uttered prophecies, so she foretold the future.

clue.text: Loud, dangerous and lively

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical direction for loud
dangerous means risky

explanation.surface: Something described as noisy, hazardous and full of energy, perhaps a party.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisky means playful and full of energy, a near synonym of lively.

clue.text: Language's sprightly return in South Carolina

definitions.note: read as 'language is', the 's being a link

indicators.note: the reversed word sits inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: SC is the postal abbreviation for South Carolina

indicators.note: the synonym for sprightly is turned round

parts.note: sprightly can mean airy, light and lively

explanation.surface: A language makes a lively comeback in South Carolina.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' looks like part of the story of the language's revival, but it turns the synonym for sprightly backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Syriac is an Aramaic dialect, once a major literary tongue of early Christianity in the Middle East.

clue.text: Supplier of publicity about terrible voyeur

indicators.note: the publicity letters go around the rearranged word

parts.note: PR, public relations, is publicity

indicators.note: terrible signals that the letters of voyeur are in a bad state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A firm supplies publicity about a dreadful peeping Tom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' reads as a judgement on the voyeur, but it signals that his letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A purveyor is someone who provides goods, especially food, as a trade.

clue.text: Gradually release second person in right place

indicators.note: the pronoun goes inside the word for right

parts.note: pat means exactly right or at the right point, as in 'off pat'
you is the pronoun of the second person

explanation.surface: Instructions to let something go slowly, such as rope, with a second person standing in the correct spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay out a rope is to let it slacken little by little, so it is released gradually.

clue.text: Strong American abandoning Tao

indicators.note: the abbreviation for American leaves the phrase

parts.note: Tao is Chinese for the way, the path of Taoism

explanation.surface: A powerful American turns his back on Taoism.
explanation.walkthrough: Tao translates as 'the way', so the leaf is the phrase THE WAY with one A dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Thews are muscles, so a thewy person is brawny and physically powerful.

clue.text: In enclosure there's shelter in weather that's icy

indicators.note: shelter is placed in the enclosure word

parts.note: a sty is a pig's enclosure
the lee is the sheltered side, out of the wind

explanation.surface: Livestock in a pen have some shelter during freezing weather.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleety weather brings sleet, half-frozen rain, so it is near-freezing and icy.

clue.text: Iron used in priest's house dining-hall

indicators.note: iron is put inside the clergyman's home

parts.note: a rectory is the house of a rector, a parish priest
FE is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: Iron is used in building the dining hall of a priest's house.
explanation.definitionFit: A refectory is a communal dining room, especially in a monastery or college.

clue.text: Still one may be found in the mountains

definitions.text: Still one may be found in the mountains

parts.note: still in the sense 'even now' is yet
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Even now, a creature might yet be found in the high mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the creature while 'Still' and 'one' build it.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of Himalayan legend is said to roam the high mountains still, undiscovered.

clue.text: Adolescent unknown to be that small

parts.note: an adolescent is a teen
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A teenager unaware of being so little.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeny is a childlike word for very small, tiny.

clue.text: Nameless junior warder is a disaster

indicators.note: without a name means the letter N, the abbreviation for name, goes

parts.note: a turnkey is a jailer, a lowly prison officer who holds the keys

explanation.surface: An anonymous junior prison guard is a complete failure.
explanation.definitionFit: In informal use a flop, especially a play or film that fails badly, is called a turkey.

clue.text: Lacking time yeast could make it light

indicators.note: what is left of the word could be made into something else, so rearrange it
the abbreviation for time is missing from the leaven word

explanation.surface: Without time to prove, the yeast could still make the bread light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking' takes T from YEAST, leaving YEAS; 'could make' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Light can mean not difficult, as in light work, so it is a synonym of undemanding.

clue.text: Cosmetic base for the old ship

parts.note: e is the base of natural logarithms
ye is the old spelling of the
a liner is a large passenger ship

explanation.surface: Make-up as a foundation for an elderly vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' is the mathematical constant e, the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is make-up applied to outline the eyes, one kind of cosmetic.

clue.text: Old man asked for heater

indicators.note: spoken out loud the slang word is matched by the heater's name

parts.note: geezer is slang for an old man

explanation.surface: An elderly man asks for a heater to be fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the water heater's name is pronounced like geezer, slang for an old man.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a geyser is a gas appliance that heats water quickly for a bath or sink.

clue.text: Bob, holding safety-pins, essentially dictated fashion

indicators.note: the sled word goes around the central letters

parts.note: a bob is a bobsleigh, a kind of sled

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so take the middle letters

explanation.surface: A bob haircut held with safety pins set the fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' suggests a haircut, but it is a bobsleigh; 'essentially' picks the two central letters of 'safety-pins', ignoring the hyphen.
explanation.definitionFit: To have styled something is to have set how it looks, so it dictated its fashion.

clue.text: Complain about month by the sea in France

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the month is read backwards

parts.note: May is a month
mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: Moaning about a month spent at the French seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by the' joins the pieces; 'about' turns MAY to YAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to yammer is to whine or grumble loudly and persistently.

clue.text: In jester's costume Thomas does somersault near meadow

indicators.note: the name turns head over heels, reading backwards

parts.note: Tom is short for Thomas
a ley is a meadow or grassland

explanation.surface: Dressed as a court jester, Thomas turns somersaults beside a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Motley is the multicoloured outfit traditionally worn by a court fool.

clue.text: Swellings in centre of blisters? Certainly

indicators.note: the central letters of the word blisters are taken

parts.note: certainly as a reply means yes

explanation.surface: Someone asks if there are swellings in the middle of the blisters and gets a firm yes.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, so these are swellings.

clue.text: Unsupported guys embrace the French

indicators.note: the ropes word wraps around the French article

parts.note: guys are ropes holding a mast or tent, also called stays
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: Men without support hug a French group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guys' here means guy ropes, not men.
explanation.definitionFit: Stays are supports such as ropes or corsets, so being without them means unsupported.

clue.text: Nimble having no children to go on railway

parts.note: SP is sine prole, Latin for without issue, used in family trees

explanation.surface: A nimble person with no kids is free to go off by train.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, sine prole, marks someone in a family tree who died without children.
explanation.definitionFit: Spry means active and lively, especially of an older person, so agile and nimble.

clue.text: This windy hen could be 20ish

indicators.note: the clue's word hen becoming ish means the EN after its H is swapped for IS

parts.note: twenty written as a word, the ish telling how it is to be changed

explanation.surface: A blustery hen might be about twenty years old.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'hen could be ish' as a swap: H stays and EN becomes IS, so in TWENTY the EN turns into IS.
explanation.definitionFit: A windy road twists and turns, so windy here means full of bends, not breezy.

clue.text: Cook young fish for Queen

parts.note: fry are young fish
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A cook prepares baby fish for the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A fryer is one who fries food, so a cook, or a pan used for frying.

clue.text: Jealous European Marshal enthralled by eager desire

indicators.note: held captive inside, so these go within the desire word

parts.note: greed is an eager desire for more
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: A European marshal, envious, is gripped by an eager longing.
explanation.definitionFit: Green-eyed means jealous, from Shakespeare's 'green-eyed monster' in Othello.
